output.summary: Approved the G1000 design (attempt 4): as approved at attempt 3, plus edit refuses a new skip of a lens while its latest record has any open finding that is not a filter-judged note (closes the join-window skip), with per-lens independence and impl-stage intent-staleness tests. Directive to implement for the reviewer's remaining non-blocking hole (a skip accepted while the lens is running with no record): approval items and the PR body must also list open findings recorded on skipped nodes, so a late finding is never invisible. Decision made by Claude (root agent) under the owner's standing delegation for Release 1; owner keeps the engine.min gate and this repository's intent wording.

responses.review_tests:1:1: fixed: took the simpler rule. D6, §5 and §17's §4.18 amendment now say edit refuses a new skip.<n> while n's latest record has any open finding that is not a note, where a note is an open finding with the verdict `note` on its filter's fresh latest record (§7). Findings that are live, waiting for the filter, or waiting for re-review all block the skip; the refusal message names them and the waiver path (status="waived" plus a note). It reuses §7's note test, so no extra liveness code. §13 journey 6 adds the test: a lens submits a material finding, filter_design has not yet run, edit --set skip.<lens> is refused, and after waiving it is accepted; a lens with only filter-judged notes can be skipped. test_design is to add this case to test_6. output.summary: Revision 4 of the parallel-lens design, one correction. D6/§5/§17 §4.18: edit now refuses a new skip.<n> while n's latest record has any open finding that is not a note (a note = open finding with verdict `note` on its filter's fresh latest record). This closes the filter's join window, where findings were open but not yet live and a skip deleted them unseen. §13 journey 6 gains the case: a skip refused before filter_design runs, accepted after a visible waiver, and allowed when only filter-judged notes remain. Non-blocking notes taken: an explicit per-lens independence test (designer/implementer start refused with `independence`) and an intent-staleness check at the impl stage. Everything else unchanged.

Approved. Revision 4's rule (edit refuses a new skip.<n> while n's latest record has any open non-note finding, where a note is judged only by a fresh filter record whose fingerprint includes the candidates) closes the join-window skip (I22). A new or unverdicted note blocks the skip, and a stale filter never counts. D6, §5, §13 journey 6 and §17 §4.18 agree, and the tests cover both sides. Prior F1/F2 stay resolved. Non-blocking notes: a lens skipped while still running (no record yet) can still submit a finding that is then dropped (end the lease on skip, or list such findings); and edit can set status=resolved instead of waived (an existing gap).

findings.text: Skip refusal misses findings waiting on the filter. D6/§5 refuse a new skip.<n> only while n has live findings, but under §7 a filtered lens's findings are not live until the filter is fresh. Between the lens submit and the filter's next fresh submit (every round, until the slowest lens finishes or indefinitely behind a crash-looping lens), `edit --set skip.<lens>` is accepted. Frontier drops skipped nodes from R (frontier.py:148), so the findings never become candidates or reopen anything. Impact: a material finding the target never saw is deleted by a one-line edit, and the human sees only 'skipped: <reason>'. That is the skip-visibility-only alternative D6 rejected (I22 / ad2). Fix: edit refuses a new skip.<n> while n's latest record has an open finding that is live or waiting for its filter (pass-1 liveness without the filter-fresh condition), or more simply any open non-note finding. Waiving first stays the visible path. Update §5, D6 and §17 §4.18, and add a test_6 case where the skip is refused before the filter runs.

output.summary: Tests are sound: the freeze is byte-identical and weakens nothing, §13 and the acceptance are fully covered, the docstring contracts match the design, and all 46 red tests fail because the feature is missing. One material design gap: edit refuses a skip only for live findings, so a lens can be skipped while its findings wait for the filter, which silently drops them (I22). Fix: refuse while the lens has findings that are live or waiting for the filter, and add a test_6 case.

spec:
Replace the default graph's single design review and single code review with independent, parallel review lenses that judge the work through abstract, philosophical questions rather than technical checklists. Ship it in plugins/zzzops/zzzops/templates/default/ and adopt it in this repository's .zzzops/ through a zzzops/policy/* branch.

Proposed lenses, each a review node with its own prompt, reviewing `design` and again reviewing `implement`:
- Intent (fidelity, not skippable): two questions. (1) Goal intent: does this solve the problem that was actually asked, faithfully to the goal's original statement and the approved design? (2) Project intent: does it serve the project's original purpose, or pull the project away from it? Look for drift, scope creep, quiet redefinition of the problem, silently dropped requirements, and goals that are locally sensible but move the project off course. This lens exists because ZzzOps itself nearly died of drift from its original intent.
- Simplicity (elegance and entropy, not skippable): is this the simplest thing that fully works? Separate essential from accidental complexity, and find what can be deleted. Check cohesion, multi-responsibility files and over-fragmentation, and whether the change leaves the codebase simpler or more tangled than it found it.
- Safety (skippable): what could this harm, and who? Security, privacy, data loss, irreversible or destructive actions, trust boundaries and abuse.
- Scale (skippable): does it hold as load, data, concurrency, users and time grow? Include performance pathologies and long-term maintenance cost.
- Experience (skippable): what is it like for the person on the other end, whether user, operator or future reader? Clarity, failure and recovery, accessibility, error messages and docs.
These five are a starting hypothesis, not the answer. Choose the final set by experiment.

Lens experiment (part of design, before approve_design):
- Write the design first. Then review it with many candidate lenses as independent reviewers, each with only its own lens prompt. Candidates: the five above, plus at least Truth/evidence (is every claim verifiable, and does it fail honestly?), Reversibility (what is hard to undo?), Coherence (does it fit the system's existing concepts?), Necessity (should this exist at all?), Adversary (how would someone break or game it?) and the old technical lenses (architecture, security, performance, concurrency, migration, UX) as a control.
- Where cheap, also replay the candidates on one or two past designs or diffs with known defects, for example reset-era review findings in the design-reset reviews/ folder, to measure recall against real misses.
- Score each lens on: material findings (ones that changed the design); findings unique to it, not raised by any other lens; false or noise findings; and cost (tokens and time). Report a table and recommend the smallest set with the best unique-material yield. Lenses that mostly duplicate others merge or drop.
- The experiment's lenses run as ad hoc reviews outside the graph (the engine does not need to support them). Its report is an artifact of design, so review_design and the owner see the evidence.
The final node list and lens set is approved at approve_design.

Mechanics, on the current engine:
- Lenses fan out from their subject and join for free: approve_design (and base) list each design lens's summary as a context input; integrate and approve_merge do the same for the code lenses.
- A finding from any lens reopens its target through the findings rule.
- review_tests stays a single general review.
- Lenses are user-configurable: a goal can skip an optional lens through `skip: {<lens node>: reason}`. The add-goal skill proposes skips at capture from the goal's risks, and any phase can raise an unforeseen risk as a blocked question so a skipped lens is unskipped. A project can also change the lens set in its own workflow.json.
- Folds in old #501 (risks choose lenses) and #380/#384 (entropy review as a lens).

Nitpick filter (owner request): reviewers tend to find something because they feel obliged to, so every review, design and code alike, passes through a filter before its findings reopen work.
- Each finding carries a materiality claim: what goes wrong if it is ignored.
- The filter separates material findings, which reopen the target, from nitpicks and preferences, which are recorded as non-blocking notes. Notes are shown to the next attempt and to approvers, but they never reopen work or count against the correction budget.
- The filter is independent of the reviewer and errs toward keeping a finding when unsure.
- Lens prompts state explicitly that approving with no findings is a good outcome.
- Options for the design to choose between: an engine rule (severity or material flag on findings; non-material findings do not reopen), a separate filter agent node per review fan-in, or both. Weigh this against R2, the removed admission gate: keep it cheap, and never let the filter silently drop a material finding.
- The lens experiment measures nit rate per lens with and without the filter.

Project intent must be defined, not inferred:
- Bootstrap must capture the project's original intent with the owner: what the project is for, who it serves, what it deliberately is not, and the principles that must survive change. It lives in a dedicated, reviewed policy artifact (for example an `intent` section of .zzzops/PROJECT.md, or a policy instruction the Intent lens declares as an input). The design decides the exact form.
- The bootstrap skill and template require it, and `validate --policy` reports it missing.
- Changing it is a policy change (a zzzops/policy/* branch, previewable with --policy-ref), never a side effect of a goal. Because the Intent lens declares it as an input, changing it stales Intent reviews on open goals.
- This repository's own intent is written in the same change, with the owner.

Small engine change in scope: re-reviews of a design document get a "what changed" pointer (records.reviewed and card.previous today only record code checkpoints), so each lens does not re-read the whole design every round. The integrate PR body should list every lens summary.

Acceptance:
- validate --policy passes for the template and this repo.
- A journey test shows lenses running in parallel; one lens's finding reopening design and the other lenses re-reviewing the new design; a skipped optional lens; a refused skip of a non-skippable lens; and approve_design presenting every lens summary.
- Every lens has a focused prompt. Reviewer independence holds per lens. Prompt budgets pass.
- The nitpick filter is tested: a nit-only review leaves its target current; a material finding still reopens it; a borderline finding is kept.
- Engine tests no longer depend on the shipped graph's node names: freeze the current 12-node graph as a test fixture.
- Bootstrap captures project intent; a missing project intent fails validate --policy; the Intent lens reads it as a declared input.
- SPEC §7, DESIGN §4.1/§10, MIGRATING.md, package.py and the bootstrap, add-goal and execute skills are updated.

Out of scope (post-MVP): lens applicability predicates in the engine, a durable requirements Q&A phase, findings targeting goal.spec, red-before-green verification (#457), PR-comment interpretation, and decomposition.

Migrated from GitHub issue #499 (plus #501, #380 and #384) after the engine reset (#740).
